title: Isometric muscle action
summary: An isometric action produces muscle tension without appreciable muscle-length change or visible joint movement. A static posture can still involve muscle force.
detailed_content: An isometric action produces muscle tension without appreciable muscle-length change or visible joint movement. A static posture can still involve muscle force.

title: Concentric muscle action
summary: In concentric loading, an active muscle shortens while overcoming an external resistance. This definition alone does not identify the active muscle in a particular exercise.

title: Eccentric muscle action
summary: In eccentric loading, an active muscle lengthens under tension while controlling an external load. A visible lowering phase must not automatically be assigned this label for every muscle.

title: Dynamic resistance is not necessarily isotonic
concept: Dynamic resistance is not necessarily isotonic
summary: The authors avoid using isotonic for dynamic resistance exercise: muscle tension changes with muscle length and the changing load moment arm. Constant external weight does not establish constant muscle tension.

title: Resistance exercise requires individual context
summary: The text bases resistance-exercise selection on examination, underlying pathology, impairments, healing stage, age, fitness and ability to participate. A textbook technique is not an individualized prescription.
detailed_content: The text bases resistance-exercise selection on examination, underlying pathology, impairments, healing stage, age, fitness and ability to participate. A textbook technique is not an individualized prescription.

precautions: Review individual condition and stage of healing before selecting or progressing resistance exercise.

title: Progressive overload is conditional
summary: Resistance intensity or exercise volume can increase training demand, but progression must account for pathology, healing, fatigue, ability and goals and allow adaptation before a further increase.
detailed_content: Resistance intensity or exercise volume can increase training demand, but progression must account for pathology, healing, fatigue, ability and goals and allow adaptation before a further increase.

precautions: Do not automatically increase load or repetitions from an animation request.
